thread.title: Apple Stock Gets Price-Target Cut, Called Good Long-Term Investment | Investor's Business Daily

author: PATRICK SEITZ
title: Apple Stock Gets Price-Target Cut, Called Good Long-Term Investment | Investor's Business Daily
text:
Amid a steep decline in valuation, Apple stock on Monday received another price-target cut from a Wall Street analyst.
X Loop Capital Markets analyst Ananda Baruah cut his price target on Apple ( AAPL ) to 225 from 259 but reiterated his buy rating.
Apple stock rose 1.4% to 174.62 on the stock market today . Since it gave disappointing guidance on Nov. 1, Apple stock has fallen 21.4% through Monday's close. The stock has traded below its 200-day moving average line for the last nine sessions.
Apple remains "an attractive long-term investment," based on its earnings power and current valuation, Baruah said.

Baruah lowered his iPhone unit sales estimates for the December and March quarters as well as calendar 2019.
He cut his iPhone unit estimate for the December quarter to 75 million from 80 million previously. The consensus estimate is 76 million units.
For the March quarter, Baruah lowered his estimate to 45 million from 55 million. Wall Street was modeling 51 million.
For calendar 2019, he now expects Apple to sell 204 million iPhone units, down from 227 million and vs. consensus expectations for 215 million.
His iPhone estimate cuts come after reports that Apple's supply chain partners, including contract manufacturer Foxconn, are lowering their production targets.
The company's midrange iPhone XR has been underperforming. Apple has cut prices for the iPhone XR in Japan to boost demand, Baruah said.
